entries.non_ste_example: Display the stack trace in the terminal after the build fails.
entries.ste_example: Show the stack trace in the terminal after the build fails.
entries.explanation: 'Display' is not approved in the STE-Code controlled terminology. The approved synonym is 'show' (see synonym table: show → NOT display, render, present). This follows P1 which requires words approved in the dictionary. P14 also applies: use American English spelling for approved words.

entries.non_ste_example: Install the container orchestration platform before you deploy the backend services.
entries.ste_example: Install Kubernetes before you deploy the backend services.
entries.explanation: 'Kubernetes' is a code-domain technical noun — it names a specific software tool in the container orchestration subject field. P5 allows technical code nouns (keywords, frameworks, tools) directly in STE-Code documentation. The descriptive phrase 'container orchestration platform' is longer, less precise, and unnecessary when the standard technical noun exists. P8 and P9 also apply: prefer short, well-known technical nouns.

entries.non_ste_example: Do a minification of the CSS bundle before you send it to the CDN.
entries.ste_example: Minify the CSS bundle before you send it to the CDN.
entries.explanation: 'Minify' is a code-domain technical verb that describes a specific build process (removing whitespace and shortening identifiers). P12 allows technical verbs in STE-Code documentation. The non-STE version turns the technical verb into a noun ('do a minification of'), which violates P13 — do not use technical verbs as nouns. Use the technical verb in its verb form.

entries.non_ste_example: The logging module transmits trace data to the application performance monitoring service.
entries.ste_example: The logging module sends trace data to Datadog.
entries.explanation: 'Datadog' is not in the STE-Code controlled terminology but it is a code-domain technical noun — the name of a specific observability tool. P6 allows non-approved words when they are code-domain technical nouns. The STE version also replaces 'transmits' with 'sends' (P1: approved synonym per the table: send → NOT transmit, dispatch). The long descriptive phrase is replaced by the precise technical noun, following P9 (prefer short, clear technical nouns).

entries.non_ste_example: Commence the relational database service before you initialize the web application.
entries.ste_example: Start PostgreSQL before you start the web application.
entries.explanation: Two P1 violations corrected. First, 'commence' and 'initialize' are not approved — the approved synonym is 'start' (see synonym table: start → NOT initiate, commence). Second, P5 allows the code-domain technical noun 'PostgreSQL' instead of the vague descriptive phrase 'relational database service.' The STE version uses precise technical nouns with approved verbs.
